## Recipe 4 — Write a CEL rule at S3 with a cost budget {#recipe-4}

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`cmd/trishula`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/trishula) + a rule pack file, any host with Go | Policy | medium | 10 min | engine · cel | cel, cost budget |

### Problem

You want one CEL rule at the S3 slot. You want a hard cost ceiling on it.
You want proof the ceiling bites, at evaluation and at compile.

### Solution

1. Copy the seed pack to a work file. Declare a budget below the rule's real cost
(the seed rule evaluates at cost 3):

```yaml
rules:
  - id: R4-BUDGET
    name: rate-shape-budget-bite
    description: 'The seed rate rule under a 2-cost ceiling'
    action: log
    costBudget: 2
    expression: |
      request.method == "POST" &&
      path.matches("/v1/chat/*") &&
      request.rate_windows["5m"].requests > 40
```

2. Run the pack. The ceiling stops every evaluation:

```bash
go run ./cmd/trishula --selftest --rules <pack-path>.yaml
```

```text
case below-threshold-no-match             match=false error=true  cost=3     FAIL detail=operation cancelled: actual cost limit exceeded
exit status 1
```

3. Check the compile side. The bundle load refuses an unusable declared budget
(the fail-closed gate):

```bash
go test ./internal/operator -run TestLoadRejectsUnusableDeclaredBudget -count=1
```

```text
ok   github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/internal/operator  <seconds>s
```

### Discussion

The budget rides the pack wire: `costBudget` sits on the rule. The policy's
`celBudget` is the fallback ceiling. Rule budget wins. A budget change re-plans
the program; it never re-compiles the module. The refusal detail names the
ceiling: `actual cost limit exceeded`. The compile-side gate rejects a pack whose
rule cannot run under its declared budget. No bundle ships on refusal.

The rule rides the S3 slot: the same rate rule the parity walk prints at S3.

### See also

- [spec §11.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#113-cel-as-the-developer-facing-dsl) — the CEL DSL. [spec §8.1](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#81-design-principles) — the cost-budget principle.
- [The seed pack](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/rules/cel/seed.yaml) — the rule form.
- [TR-17 issue #17](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/17) — hot reload + cost budgets.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, on the host clone:

- `go run ./cmd/trishula --selftest --rules <pack-budget-2>.yaml`: exit 1. Every case read
  `error=true cost=3` with `detail=operation cancelled: actual cost limit exceeded`.
- `go test ./internal/operator -run TestLoadRejectsUnusableDeclaredBudget -count=1`: ok.


## Recipe 9 — Ban an offender manually: a CEL rule with `action: ban` {#recipe-9}

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`cmd/engine/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/engine) · [`internal/operator/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/internal/operator) | Enforcement | medium | 5 min | policy + engine | ban, CEL, WAFPolicy, TR-195 |

### Problem

You watched one source hammer a route. You want to stop that source now.
You do not want to wait for a score. You want the stop to leave evidence
and to name the rule that wrote it.

### Solution

A rule pack carries one rule with `action: ban`. The matcher can say one
word: the path. The source stays on the wall as a would-ban record.

1. Write the rule pack. The action is `ban`; the match is narrow:

```yaml
rules:
  - id: OPS-MANUAL-01
    name: manual-ban
    description: stop the offender on the login route
    action: ban
    expression: |
      request.method == "POST" && path.matches("/v1/chat/*")
```

2. Ship it the way every rule ships: the ConfigMap + the `WAFPolicy` CR
   that points at the pack (Recipe 2 owns that surface). Compile and apply.
   The gate compiles the pack; the CRD carries the bundle.

```bash
kubectl -n trishula apply -f rulepack-manual-ban.yaml
kubectl -n trishula apply -f wafpolicy-with-ban.yaml
```

3. Probe the route from the offender source. The response carries the
   decision, the rule id and the body:

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST "http://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions?q=x"
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-Trishula-Decision: ban
X-Trishula-Hop: engine
X-Trishula-Rule: OPS-MANUAL-01

banned by OPS-MANUAL-01
```

4. Read the ban evidence. Start the engine with `--ban-evidence`, then
   read the JSONL line the match wrote:

```bash
kubectl -n trishula logs deploy/trishula-engine | tail -3
```

```text
would-ban 192.0.2.10 tier=manual-rule score=0 sig={Class:manual-rule Paths:[/v1/chat/completions]}
```

5. Lift the ban. Remove the rule from the pack and re-apply. The next
   bundle no longer names the rule, so the match disappears. The scored
   window for that source decays on its own clock.

### Discussion

`action: ban` folds with the response ladder as a block class on the
inside and a direct would-ban out the back. The record carries the
`manual-rule` tier and the signature (`class`, `paths`). The same record
reaches the enforcer the scored path uses; a deployed enforcer publishes
the kernel row the same way. The verdict signals name the rule: the
consult-signal test in [#252](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/252)
pins `verdict.action=ban`, `verdict.rules=OPS-MANUAL-01` and
`verdict.dos.sig`.

Keep the match narrow. `action: ban` never waits for a score; a wide
expression bans whole routes. The fail-open posture: a failed evidence
write stays logged; the block decision stands.

### See also

- [spec §13.7](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#137-dos-response-posture-who-does-what) — the manual and the automatic paths.
- [spec §13.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#133-the-ban-algorithm-scoredwindowban-v1-specified) — the scored path the record shares.
- [Issue #237](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/237) — the DoS/ban stream. [PR #248](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/248) — the ban surface. [PR #252](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/252) — the signals.
- [Recipe 6 — the scored ban ladder.](recipes-kernel.html)
- [Recipe 10 — the signature the record carries.](recipes-kernel.html)

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@798beb1](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/aac9da071568c1eed4977cea1623a0c642b21992)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25:

  ([#248](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/248)).
- The consult-signal run: the verdict span carries the action, the rule id
  and the signature ([#252](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/252)).
- The in-VM acceptance for the kernel legs: recorded on
  [#253](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/253) with the run
  transcript.


## Recipe 11 — Enable bot detection and the challenge: the consensus verdict, the redirect, the proof {#recipe-11}

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`internal/engine/botdef/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/internal/engine/botdef) · [`cmd/engine/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/engine) | Enforcement | medium | 10 min | policy + engine | bot, challenge, TR-197 |

### Problem

A credential-stuffing bot spreads login attempts across one source: no single
request carries a bad string. You want one response for it: a wall that costs
the client work, not a permanent ban. You want evidence of what answered.

### Solution

Two surfaces ship the flow: the detector consensus resolves `challenge`
(two distinct families at or above the confidence floor), and the engine
answers with a signed redirect that costs one small hash probe.

1. Generate the signing key and start the engine with it. No key = the
   challenge verdict refuses (the gate never pretends to challenge):

```bash
CHALLENGE_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
./engine --upstream http://app:8080 \
         --bundle /etc/trishula/bundle.json \
         --challenge-key "$CHALLENGE_KEY" -listen :8080
```

2. Point the policy at the wall. The CRD carries the action today:
   `defaultAction: challenge`, or the bot consensus resolves it when two
   detector families agree per source:

```yaml
spec:
  defaultAction: challenge
```

3. Probe. The consensus verdict answers `429` with the redirect:

```bash
curl -s -i "http://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions"
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Location: /__trishula/challenge?token=<payload>.<hmac>
X-Trishula-Decision: challenge
```

4. Read the problem. The hop prints the signed probe: the salt, the
   difficulty, the problem token. Nothing is consumed by reading it:

```bash
curl -s "http://<gateway>/__trishula/challenge?token=<tok>"
```

```text
problem-token=<tok>
salt=<hex>
diff=16
```

5. Solve. The nonce whose `sha256(salt:nonce)` starts with 16 zero bits
   is the answer; ~65k hashes, under a second on a laptop. The solve
   consumes both tokens once and grants the pass cookie:

```text
challenge verified; retry the original request
Set-Cookie: trishula_pass=<token>; HttpOnly; Max-Age=600
```

6. Retry the original request with the cookie. The consult reads the
   grant back and forwards the request for the cookie's TTL. A client
   that never solves stays on the wall: every attempt re-answers `429`.

### Discussion

The token = the payload + the HMAC-SHA256 over it. The expiry lives in
the payload (a 10-minute TTL); a nonce marks one-shot use: a consumed
token refuses the second solve. A tampered payload, a dropped byte or a
wrong key refuses with the named reason in the hop's log. A past-expiry
token refuses identically — the exit criterion "the replay beyond the
TTL refuses" holds two ways.

Fail-open stays off here on purpose: a challenge that cannot mint is a
deterministic `403`, never a silent pass. The proof probe stays small by
default (16 bits); the difficulty is a constant in
[`internal/engine/challenge/eow.go`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/internal/engine/challenge/eow.go)
until the CRD knob ships.

### See also

- [spec §12.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#122-verdict-integration) — the challenge verdict in the ladder.
- [spec §13.7](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#137-dos-response-posture-who-does-what) — where the challenge sits beside the ban path.
- [Issue #239](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/239) — the stream. [PR #256](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/256) · [PR #258](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/258) — the leaves.
- Recipe 9 above — the manual `action: ban` for the confirmed offender.
